name: Act of March 1, 1889 ratifying the Creek agreement of January 19, 1889
aka: Creek cession of the Oklahoma lands
promises: Royce records that the Creeks ceded to the United States the half of their domain lying west of the division line set by the treaty of June 14, 1866, and all claims to other lands except their domain east of that line.
The Indian Claims Commission records that the United States agreed to pay $2,280,857.10 for the cession.
compensation: The Indian Claims Commission, quoting its own earlier findings, states that the consideration of $2,280,857.10 was paid to the Creek Nation under the 1889 agreement.
today: In Docket 167 the Commission (1963) considered 1,198.99 acres lying east of the dividing line that the Court of Claims had held were released by the 1889 agreement; that land is outside the ceded area mapped here. Docket 167 ended in a $50,000 compromise in 1971. Royce records that the President's proclamation of March 23, 1889 opened the ceded lands to settlement.

openQuestions: treaties.json lists the Poarch Band of Creeks, Alabama, as a present-day tribe for this record; the 1889 agreement concerned the Creek Nation's domain in Indian Territory, and no source here ties the Poarch Band to it.
The Muscogee (Creek) Nation's own account of the 1889 cession was not located.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Creek, Creek 1889 cession; Creek Nation v. United States, 93 Ct. Cl. 561 (1941) dismissed the 1,198.99-acre claim on the 1889 agreement (already recorded via Docket 167); 77 Ct. Cl. 159 (1933) concerns land east of the line put in the Sac and Fox reservation; 63 Ct. Cl. 270 (1927) concerns the 1814 treaty; nothing new on the ceded land.
